topic: The Fundamental Bridge: Connecting Derivatives and Integrals

sections.title: The Hook: Speed vs. Distance
lecture_lines: A robot runs: speed is the instantaneous derivative.
Area under the speed curve is total distance.
These processes are inversely connected, remarkably.
animations: Show two cars (red A, blue B) on horizontal track.
Label car A 'Constant Speed', car B 'Acceleration'.
Animate cars moving across screen left to right.
Highlight area under car B's speed path in yellow.
Display text 'Distance is Area under Curve' in white.

sections.title: Review of Prerequisite: The Derivative as a 'Zoom'
lecture_lines: Derivatives measure the instantaneous rate of change.
Imagine zooming into a curve to see slope.
Slope defines the rate at that specific moment.
animations: Plot y=x^2 in white on coordinate plane.
Create red point moving along the curve.
Display tangent line as blue line at point.
Zoom in on point until curve looks like line.
Label slope 'dy/dx' in green near tangent.

sections.title: The Integral as 'Summation'
lecture_lines: Integrals accumulate many tiny slices into one sum.
Think of filling a tank over time.
Adding these slices gives the total amount.
animations: Plot function f(x) in white.
Draw multiple thin rectangles (blue) filling area.
Animate width of rectangles shrinking to zero.
Show integral symbol ∫ f(x) dx in orange.
Sum areas of all rectangles to fill total.

sections.title: The Fundamental Bridge
lecture_lines: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations.
They work like adding and subtracting numbers.
One builds up, the other breaks down.
F of x differentiated becomes f of x.
F of x integrated returns to original form.
animations: Show velocity v(t) curve in blue.
Highlight area slice (yellow) under velocity.
Show area growing as accumulation of velocity.
Introduce d/dt and ∫ as inverse pair.
Demonstrate ∫[v(t)dt] = s(t) relationship.

sections.title: Summary & Application
lecture_lines: The Integral recovers the original anti-derivative.
Solve complex physics using this inverse relationship.
Fuel rate leads to exact rocket altitude.
animations: Draw plot showing rocket fuel consumption rate.
Fill area under curve to show altitude.
Flash result 'Final Altitude' in yellow color.
